title: Analyst research assistant for the internal report library
brief:
We want a research assistant for our 50 internal analysts. They spend hours hunting through our own research reports - about 4,000 PDFs going back six years, plus the weekly market notes - to answer questions such as "what did we say about warehouse automation payback last year" or "which reports cover cold-chain logistics in Vietnam". Today they search by filename and ask whoever wrote the report.

The assistant should answer questions from those reports and cite the page it took each statement from, so an analyst can open the source and check it. It must never take any action: no posting, no editing a report, no sending anything, no updating any system of record. If the reports do not answer the question it should say so plainly rather than guess.

Not every analyst may see every report. Some client work is restricted to the team that did it, and the assistant must respect those entitlements.

We expect roughly 3,000 questions a month from the 50 analysts. English only. We are not in a regulated industry, but an answer that is confidently wrong would cost us more client trust than a slow answer ever would. Success looks like an analyst getting a cited answer in under two minutes where it takes about twenty minutes today.

assumptions.statement: The report library exposes a read-only search index with per-report entitlement metadata, so the retriever can filter by what the asking analyst may see before any passage is read.
assumptions.why: Every control in this design rests on filtering at retrieval rather than after drafting.
assumptions.validation: Confirm the index exposes entitlement fields and that they are maintained with the report.

assumptions.statement: Each report carries a version and a superseded-by field, so a superseded edition can be marked rather than quoted as current.
assumptions.why: Quoting a withdrawn report as current is the failure analysts said would cost the most trust.
assumptions.validation: Sample fifty reports and check both fields are present and correct.

assumptions.statement: Page numbers in the extracted text match the page numbers an analyst sees when opening the PDF, including for reports scanned from print.
assumptions.why: A citation an analyst cannot follow to the right page is not a citation.
assumptions.validation: Spot-check 100 citations across born-digital and scanned reports.

assumptions.statement: An illustrative first-release volume of 3,000 questions a month, about 150 a working day, with a peak of three times the mean in the week after a major report lands.
assumptions.why: Volume drives the model budget and the size of the review sample.
assumptions.validation: Measure actual question volume during the shadow phase.

assumptions.statement: Analyst identity and team membership come from the corporate directory at session start and are not supplied by the analyst or inferred by the model.
assumptions.why: Entitlement filtering is only as trustworthy as the identity it filters on.
assumptions.validation: Confirm the directory integration and that no identity field is user-editable.

assumptions.statement: A baseline of about twenty minutes to find a cited answer by hand, taken from the brief and not yet measured.
assumptions.why: The headline KPI compares against it, so it must be measured before any claim is made.
assumptions.validation: Time twenty real questions before the shadow phase starts.

items.title: Success measures and end conditions
items.description: The outcome the business is buying, and when a case is finished.
items.reasoning: An end condition that includes a decline is what keeps the system honest.

sources.passage: Success looks like an analyst getting a cited answer in under two minutes where it takes about twenty minutes today.

data.value: Success is a cited answer an analyst accepts without correction, in under two minutes against a hand-search baseline of about twenty minutes. A case ends in one of two ways: an answer with a citation per claim, or a decline naming what was searched. Both count as a finished case; only a confidently wrong answer counts as a failure.

data.value: No sector regulation applies. The binding constraint is commercial confidentiality: client work is restricted to the team that did it, and a passage from a restricted report must never reach an analyst without entitlement. The assistant holds a read-only credential and has no write path to any system. English only in the first release.

items.title: Why an assistant fits
items.description: Whether this needs an agent at all.
items.reasoning: The honest answer is that most of the value is better search, and the design says so.

sources.passage: They spend hours hunting through our own research reports

data.choice: A retrieval assistant, with a model only for reading the question and composing the answer. Most of the gain is entitlement-aware search over 4,000 reports.
alternatives: A plain search box with better indexing, no model at all
A fine-tuned model trained on the report corpus
data.tradeoffs: Plain search is cheaper and would capture much of the value, but leaves the analyst to read twenty passages. Fine-tuning bakes the corpus into weights, which makes citation impossible and staleness invisible, so it is rejected outright for this use.
data.blastRadius: An unhelpful answer wastes an analyst's time; it cannot change any record.
data.approvalRule: No approval step: this component takes no action on any system of record, so there is nothing to approve. The analyst remains accountable for anything published from the answer.
data.leastPrivilege: The service holds one read-only credential scoped to the report index.

items.title: Retrieve, gate, draft, check
items.description: The shape of the pipeline.
items.reasoning: Putting the sufficiency gate before the drafter is what makes a decline possible.

sources.passage: The assistant should answer questions from those reports and cite the page it took each statement from, so an analyst can open the source and check it.

data.choice: A fixed four-stage pipeline: filtered retrieval, a code sufficiency gate, a model draft, then a code citation check that can fail the whole answer.
alternatives: A single model call given the passages and asked to cite its sources
An agent loop free to search repeatedly until it is satisfied
data.tradeoffs: One model call is simpler but makes the model the judge of its own evidence, which is the failure in FM3. A free search loop has no bounded cost and no point at which sufficiency is decided, so there is no principled moment to decline. Override needs a named owner.

items.title: Entitlement in the query
items.description: Where the access decision happens.
items.reasoning: Filtering after drafting means the restricted text was already in the model's context.

sources.passage: Some client work is restricted to the team that did it, and the assistant must respect those entitlements.

data.choice: The retriever filters by the analyst's directory groups inside the query, and a separate code check re-tests every returned passage before drafting.

Trust the retriever's filter and skip the second check
data.tradeoffs: Filtering afterwards puts restricted text into the model's context, where a summary can leak it without quoting it. Skipping the second check leaves one point of failure in front of the highest-severity risk.
data.blastRadius: A failure here is a confidentiality breach, which is why there are two independent checks.

items.title: From PDF to a citable passage
items.description: Extraction and chunking, chosen together.
items.reasoning: Both are constrained by the same requirement: an analyst must be able to open the cited page.

sources.passage: about 4,000 PDFs going back six years

data.choice: Extract text with page numbers, including the scanned earlier years, then chunk by section carrying the page, version and superseded-by marker on every chunk.
alternatives: A plain PDF text library with fixed-size chunks and no page metadata
data.tradeoffs: A plain library is free and fine for born-digital reports but returns nothing for the scanned years, and fixed-size chunks cannot cite a page. items.title: Question interpreter model
items.description: A small model turns a question into a query and an answer shape.
items.reasoning: This step reads one short sentence and emits three fields; a larger tier buys nothing.

sources.passage: Today they search by filename and ask whoever wrote the report.

data.rationale: Short input, structured output, no judgement about evidence. Standard tier rejected: on fifty sample questions it produced the same query terms.

items.title: Answer drafter model
items.description: A standard model composes the answer from the retrieved passages.
items.reasoning: Composing prose that stays inside the given passages is the one place a larger tier earns its cost.

sources.passage: cite the page it took each statement from

data.rationale: The draft must stay inside the supplied passages and attribute each claim. Small tier rejected: it merged claims across passages, which the citation check then rejected, raising the failure rate rather than lowering cost. Reasoning tier rejected: no multi-step inference here.
data.fineTuneWhen: Not justified now. Only if citation-check failures stay high after prompt work, with a labelled set of rejected drafts.

items.title: A superseded report is quoted as current
items.description: Wrong or stale source. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 144.
items.reasoning: The library keeps earlier editions, so a retrieval that ignores version will find both.

sources.passage: Each report carries a version and a superseded-by field, so a superseded edition can be marked rather than quoted as current.

data.effect: An analyst repeats a figure we have since withdrawn, to a client.
data.cause: The index returns a superseded edition and nothing in the answer marks it as superseded.
data.control: C2 returns the version and supersededBy field with every passage; C5 marks any claim drawn from a superseded edition and the answer carries the marker where the analyst reads it.
data.detectionMethod: EV3 asserts the marker on a superseded passage; EV9 samples live answers for unmarked superseded citations.
data.action: Owner: Head of Research Operations. Release gate: no release until EV3 passes and a 100-answer sample shows zero unmarked superseded citations.
data.metric: Share of answers citing a superseded edition without a marker.
data.kpi: Client trust: an answer an analyst can rely on without re-checking.

items.title: A claim reaches the analyst with no citation
items.description: Missing citation. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 189.
items.reasoning: The drafter writes fluent prose and the joining sentences it adds carry no passage.

sources.passage: cite the page it took each statement from

data.effect: The analyst cannot check a statement and either trusts it or discards the whole answer.
data.cause: The drafter produces a claim with no passageId, or one naming a passage that was never retrieved.
data.control: C5 rejects any claim whose passage was not in the retrieved set, and an uncited claim fails the whole answer rather than being silently removed from it.
data.detectionMethod: EV1 and EV4 assert the rejection; EV10 alerts on the live rate of answers failing the citation check.
data.action: Owner: Research Platform Lead. Release gate: EV1 and EV4 pass, and the shadow phase shows no answer reaching an analyst with an uncited claim.
data.metric: Count of claims with no verified passage per 1,000 answers.
data.kpi: Client trust: an answer an analyst can rely on without re-checking.

items.title: The assistant answers from outside the corpus
items.description: An answer outside the corpus. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 160.
items.reasoning: The model knows a plausible figure from pre-training and fills the gap with it.

sources.passage: If the reports do not answer the question it should say so plainly rather than guess.

data.effect: A number that was never in our research is presented as our research.
data.cause: Retrieval returns weak passages and the drafter completes the answer from its own knowledge.
data.control: C6 decides sufficiency in code before the drafter runs, and C5 then requires a retrieved passage behind every claim, so a claim from outside the corpus has nothing to cite.
data.detectionMethod: EV2 and EV4 assert it on fixtures; EV7 measures it offline on a labelled set.
data.action: Owner: Head of Research. Release gate: EV2 and EV4 pass and the offline unsupported-claim rate is below 1 per cent before any analyst sees output.
data.metric: Unsupported-claim rate on the labelled offline set.
data.kpi: Client trust: an answer an analyst can rely on without re-checking.

items.title: Prompt injection carried in a report
items.description: Prompt injection through documents. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 120.
items.reasoning: Reports are written by people and occasionally pasted from elsewhere; the text is not trusted input.

sources.passage: answer questions from those reports

data.effect: Text inside a document steers the assistant into ignoring its own rules.
data.cause: A retrieved passage contains instruction-shaped text and the drafter treats it as an instruction.
data.control: C8 neutralises instruction-shaped text in every passage before the drafter sees it and flags the passage; the drafter never receives document text as an instruction.
data.detectionMethod: EV5 asserts the neutralisation on a planted fixture; EV8 is an offline adversarial set.
data.action: Owner: IT Security. Release gate: EV5 passes and the adversarial set shows no instruction followed.
data.metric: Count of injected instructions followed per adversarial run.
data.kpi: Confidentiality: nothing leaves the analyst's entitlement.

items.title: A restricted passage reaches an analyst without entitlement
items.description: Leaking content the reader may not see; an access control failure. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 160.
items.reasoning: Entitlement data and directory membership change, and a stale cache is enough to leak.

sources.passage: Some client work is restricted to the team that did it, and the assistant must respect those entitlements.

data.effect: Client-confidential work reaches someone outside the team that did it.
data.cause: The retriever's entitlement filter is stale, wrong, or bypassed by a cached result.
data.control: C2 filters inside the query so a restricted passage is never retrieved, and C3 re-checks every returned passage against the directory and drops any that fails.
data.detectionMethod: EV6 asserts the drop on a cross-team fixture; EV8 and EV9 sample live answers for out-of-entitlement citations.
data.action: Owner: IT Security. Release gate: EV6 passes, and no out-of-entitlement citation appears in the shadow phase. A single live occurrence stops the service.
data.metric: Count of citations outside the asking analyst's entitlement.
data.kpi: Confidentiality: nothing leaves the analyst's entitlement.

items.title: A confident answer when the corpus is silent
items.description: A confident answer when the corpus is silent. Hypothetical S/O/D: severity 1 negligible to 10 catastrophic; occurrence 1 rare to 10 frequent; detection 1 caught before harm to 10 rarely detected. Scores prioritise review, not probability. RPN 126.
items.reasoning: Declining feels like failure, so a system tuned for helpfulness will answer anyway.

sources.passage: If the reports do not answer the question it should say so plainly rather than guess.

data.effect: The analyst acts on an answer the library never supported and does not know to check it.
data.cause: The sufficiency threshold is too loose, or sufficiency is inferred from the drafter's confidence.
data.control: C6 decides sufficiency from a stated rule over the retrieved passages, never from the drafter's confidence, and routes to a decline that names the searched scope.
data.detectionMethod: EV2 asserts the decline; EV7 measures the decline rate offline and EV9 samples it live.
data.action: Owner: Head of Research. Release gate: EV2 passes and the offline decline rate is within the expected band before release; a collapsing decline rate blocks it.
data.metric: Decline rate, and the share of declines an analyst agrees with on review.
data.kpi: Client trust: an answer an analyst can rely on without re-checking.

assumptions: Duplicate or concurrent write, uncertain commit and false completion are inapplicable: this design has no write node, no write action class and a read-only credential with no write scope configured, so there is no effect to duplicate, leave uncertain or falsely confirm.
Human queue and SLA failure are inapplicable: no step waits for a person. A case that cannot be answered declines immediately rather than queueing, so no work can age in a queue.

Tool timeout is covered by contract rather than by a register entry: every node states a timeout and a failureDisposition that returns a decline, and an index timeout is an explicit INDEX_UNAVAILABLE status on C2 rather than an empty result that reads as a silent library.

items.title: A supported question is answered with a citation for every claim
items.description: The positive answer case: two passages support two claims, and both claims carry a report and page.
items.reasoning: This is the shape of a good answer, and the baseline every negative case mutates.

data.input: {"questionText": "What did we say about warehouse automation payback last year?", "analystId": "AN7", "teamIds": ["LOGISTICS"], "answerShape": "FIGURE", "safePassages": [{"passageId": "P11", "reportId": "R-2025-014", "page": 12, "version": "2", "supersededBy": null, "text": "Warehouse automation payback averaged 3.4 years across the eleven sites we reviewed."}, {"passageId": "P12", "reportId": "R-2024-131", "page": 7, "version": "1", "supersededBy": null, "text": "Payback shortened to 2.9 years where the site already ran a WMS."}]}

data.kpi: Client trust: an answer an analyst can rely on without re-checking.
data.target: 100 per cent of claims carry a verifiable citation; zero writes.
data.testSet: Planned synthetic fixture for the research corpus; it specifies the test and has not been executed against a built system.

data.gate: Baseline must be measured on twenty real questions before the shadow phase starts; a target claimed against an unmeasured baseline is not evidence.
data.experiment: Compare the assistant's cited answer against the same analyst's hand search on the same question.

items.title: Answers accepted without correction
items.description: Whether analysts trust what comes back.
items.reasoning: Speed with a wrong answer is worse than the status quo, so the quality KPI sits beside the time one.

sources.passage: an answer that is confidently wrong would cost us more client trust than a slow answer ever would

data.businessKpi: Share of answered questions the analyst accepts without correcting a claim or a citation: baseline unknown, there is no system today, so it is collected from the first week of the shadow phase -> target above 85 per cent by the end of the pilot.
aiMetrics: Unsupported-claim rate (EV7); share of sampled claims the cited page does not support (EV9).
data.phase: Collected in shadow, gated at general release.
data.gate: No general release until the pilot shows acceptance above 85 per cent with the unsupported-claim rate under 1 per cent.
data.experiment: Reviewers mark each sampled answer accepted, corrected or rejected, with the reason.

items.title: Shadow phase
items.description: The assistant answers, and only the reviewing analysts see it.
items.reasoning: Entry and exit evidence that does not require the results of the phase it gates.

sources.passage: A baseline of about twenty minutes to find a cited answer by hand, taken from the brief and not yet measured.

data.businessKpi: No business KPI is claimed in shadow; it exists to collect the R1 and R2 baselines.
aiMetrics: EV7 and EV8 pass; EV9 sampling runs at fifty a week.
data.phase: Shadow: four weeks, questions answered but shown only to the reviewing analysts.
data.gate: Entry: both offline sets pass and the R1 baseline is measured. Exit: four weeks of EV9 sampling with zero entitlement findings and zero unmarked superseded citations.
data.experiment: Not an experiment; this phase collects the baseline the later comparison needs.

items.title: Pilot with one team, then all fifty analysts
items.description: One team of analysts uses it for real work, then the rest.
items.reasoning: A confidentiality failure is contained to one team if it happens, and that team knows to watch for it.

sources.passage: We expect roughly 3,000 questions a month from the 50 analysts.

data.businessKpi: R1 under four minutes and R2 above 70 per cent within the pilot team before widening.
aiMetrics: EV9 weekly; EV10 alerting live with named owners.
data.phase: Pilot: six weeks with the logistics team, then all 50 analysts.
data.gate: Entry: shadow exit met. Exit to full release: six weeks with no entitlement finding, R2 above 70 per cent, and the decline rate inside its band. A single out-of-entitlement citation returns to shadow.
data.experiment: Compare pilot-team time-to-answer against the same team's measured baseline.

items.title: Does a decline beat a hedged answer?
items.description: The one genuine open question: whether analysts prefer a decline or a caveated partial answer.
items.reasoning: The design assumes a decline is better; that assumption is worth testing rather than asserting.

sources.passage: If the reports do not answer the question it should say so plainly rather than guess.

data.businessKpi: Share of analysts who rate the response useful, decline against hedged answer.
aiMetrics: Decline rate; usefulness rating; follow-up question rate after each response type.
data.phase: Runs inside the pilot, from week three.
data.gate: Only runs once EV2 passes, so both arms are built on a working sufficiency gate. The hedged arm still carries a citation for every claim; it is not permission to answer without evidence.
data.experiment: Split by question, not by analyst: half the insufficient cases return a decline naming the searched scope, half return what was found with an explicit statement of what was missing.

items.title: Named owners
items.description: Who owns what, by name of role.
items.reasoning: Every gate above names an owner; this card is where they are collected.

sources.passage: We want a research assistant for our 50 internal analysts.

data.businessKpi: Not a KPI card: it records accountability for the gates above.
aiMetrics: Each owner receives the metric for their own gate, not a shared dashboard.
data.gate: No phase advances without its named owner recorded as having seen the exit evidence.
data.owner: Head of Research owns answer quality; IT Security owns entitlement and injection; Research Platform Lead owns availability and the live alerts; Head of Research Operations owns the library and the time-to-answer KPI.

items.title: Build handoff
items.description: What a coding agent receives, and what it must not infer from it.
items.reasoning: The boundary is the whole point of this design, so the handoff restates it.

sources.passage: It must never take any action

acceptanceCriteria: Every claim returned to an analyst resolves to a passage that was actually retrieved for that question; an answer containing an uncited claim is rejected whole (EV1, EV4).
A question the retrieved passages do not support returns a decline naming the searched scope, with zero citations (EV2).
No passage outside the asking analyst's entitlement reaches the drafter or the rendered answer (EV6, EV8).
Instruction-shaped text inside a report is neutralised and flagged, and changes no answer (EV5).
A claim drawn from a superseded edition is marked with the superseding report (EV3).
The service holds a read-only credential. No code path writes to any system of record, and the write scope is not configured, not merely unused.
data.buildInstructions: Build the four stages as separate deployable units behind one service: entitlement-filtered retrieval (C2) with its access re-check (C3), the instruction guard (C8) and sufficiency gate (C6), the drafter (C4), and the citation check (C5) with the renderer (C7). Load one milestone file at a time. Treat every H assumption as a blocker until the owner confirms it; H1, H2 and H5 block launch. Do not add a write path, a cache that outlives a session, or a feedback loop that stores the analyst's question against their name, none of which this design authorises.

presentation.scopeSummary: The first release answers questions from the 4,000 report PDFs and the weekly market notes, in English, for the 50 internal analysts. It writes nothing: no posting, no editing, no sending, no updating any system of record. Anything outside the library is out of scope and returns a decline.

taskLabels.T4: Decline, and say what was searched

milestones.title: Retrieve only what this analyst may see
acceptanceCriteria: A passage outside the asking analyst's entitlement is never returned by the retriever and is dropped again by the access check (EV6).
The service runs on a read-only credential; the write scope is not configured.
Entitlement comes from the directory at session start and is never taken from the request.

milestones.title: Decide whether the library can answer
acceptanceCriteria: Instruction-shaped text inside a passage is neutralised and flagged before the drafter runs (EV5).
Sufficiency is decided by a stated rule over the retrieved passages, never by the drafter (EV2).
An insufficient case returns a decline naming the searched scope, with zero citations.

milestones.title: Answer, and prove every citation
acceptanceCriteria: Every claim resolves to a retrieved passage, and an uncited claim fails the whole answer (EV1, EV4).
A claim from a superseded edition is marked with the superseding report (EV3).
What the analyst reads is exactly what passed the citation check.
